scenes.title: CREATE TABLE
scenes.narration: CREATE TABLE defines a new table, spelling out its columns, data types, and constraints.

scenes.title: Defining a table
bullets: Names the table and its columns
Assigns a data type to each column
scenes.narration: CREATE TABLE declares a new table along with the columns it will hold. Each column is given a data type that governs what values it can store. Constraints such as PRIMARY KEY and NOT NULL enforce rules that keep the data valid.

scenes.title: Creating a table
scenes.narration: This statement creates a customers table with three columns. The id column is an integer marked as the primary key, uniquely identifying each row. The name must always be provided thanks to NOT NULL, while created_at stores a date.

scenes.title: From definition to table
steps: Empty table is ready for data
scenes.narration: You begin by listing each column with its name and data type. Keys and constraints are then added to enforce integrity. Running the statement creates an empty table, ready to receive rows.

scenes.text: A thoughtful CREATE TABLE with clear types and constraints prevents bad data from ever entering.
scenes.narration: Design your CREATE TABLE with precise data types and constraints, since a strong definition keeps invalid data out from the very start.
